filter.description:
Optionally apply filter(s) to narrow down the result set. Valid filters vary
depending on the primary resource of endpoint being queried. For example, if you
are querying /groups (i.e. primary resource = Group), filters with the format
```filter[group][...]``` are valid, and filters with the format
```filter[user][...]``` are invalid, since they are not narrowing down the current
result set of Groups.

In general, you can filter by most columns. You can additionally filter directly
on some models. Model operations vary per model, but in general they perform an
optimized ```ilike()``` on a subset of columns.

| Operator   | Description                                     | Supported Input Types | Supported Usage             |
|------------|-------------------------------------------------|-----------------------|-----------------------------|
| eq         | Equal                                           | str, int, bool, date  | Column, Model (UserType)    |
| neq        | Not equal                                       | str, int, bool, date  | Column, Model (UserType)    |
| ieq        | Equal                                           | str, int, bool, date  | Column                      |
| ineq       | Not equal                                       | str, int, bool, date  | Column                      |
| lt         | Less than                                       | str, int, bool, date  | Column                      |
| le         | Less than or equal                              | str, int, bool, date  | Column                      |
| gt         | Greater than                                    | str, int, bool, date  | Column                      |
| ge         | Greater than or equal                           | str, int, bool, date  | Column                      |
| in         | Specify multiple values, case insensitive       | str, int              | Column, Model (UserType)    |
| notin      | Specify *not* multiple values, case insensitive | str, int              | Column, Model (UserType)    |
| like       | Pattern matching, case sensitive                | str                   | Column, Model (Group, User) |
| ilike      | Pattern matching, case insensitive              | str                   | Column, Model (Group, User) |
| startswith | Matches strings starting with input             | str                   | Column                      |
| endswith   | Matches strings ending with input               | str                   | Column                      |
| contains   | Substring matching                              | str                   | Column                      |
| and        | Logical AND                                     | 1 or more operands    | N/A                         |
| or         | Logical OR                                      | 1 or more operands    | N/A                         |
| not        | Logical NOT                                     | 1 or more operands    | N/A                         |

### Filtering on Columns:
* filter[group][id]=in(2,11)

page.description:
Optionally specify the range of objects to be included in the response.
The general form is: ```page[limit]=*number*&page[after]=*id*``` or ```page[limit]=*number*&page[before]=*id*```.
The API follows *seek*/*cursor* style pagination. For API to serve previous or next pages of results, it needs to know some information about the last or first rows that the client has.
For *every* single page request (besides the very first page of results), the API needs to know the id of the target row. The other data API needs to properly get the desired page depends on one other factor -- sorting. If the result set is sorted by some column, the API will need to know the value of that column from the target row.
For example, if we search for groups and tell the API to sort the result by groups' names, ```?sort[group]=name```, then to get the next page of results, we need to tell the API the id and the name from the last row. For example, ```?sort[group]=name&page[after]=12,last_group_name```. Same logic applies to the previous page. The ```after``` and ```before``` conditions are non-inclusive.
In case the the results are sorted by id, implictly or explicitly, only one item is expected. For example, ```?sort[group]=id&page[after]=12```.

If some or no page parameters provided, the default value for the missing parameter will be used. The page limit (size) is assumed to be **100** and the starting offset (id) is **0**. The minimal value for limit is **1**, the maximal value is **1000**. ```after``` and ```before``` expect the ids to be positive integers.

**Note**: it is possible to provide *both* ```before``` and ```after``` conditions (with and without sorting condition), like ```?page[before]=5&page[after]=2```. In this case, the result will contain a slice of items the range (after; before).
page.name: page

post.description:
Create a new group with the given fields.
Notification will be sent based on the notification type chosen for the group. Notifications: "audit", "expiration", "leave", "welcome". If no email notifications are provided, "expiration" warnings is used as default.
Mandatory attributes:
  * Group's name
  * Description
  * Targets (at least one valid target)
  * Owner. The requestor becomes the owner of the Group by default. The group needs a minimun of 2 owners (any combination of user and group owners).

Validation and constrains:

  1. Group's name should be unique.

  2. Group's name should be between 3 and 64 characters.

  3. Group's name should contain only alphanumeric characters and characters '.', '_', '-' (_dot_, _underscore_, _dash_).

  4. Group's description is not empty and is shorter than 256 chars (inclusive).

  5. Target name should be valid.

  6. User owners and parent groups should have valid ids, and they should exist in the system. If their ids are invalid, the group creation will be rejected.

  7. Adding user members or child groups is disallowed as a part of the create call. Other endpoints dedicated to these operations should be used.

Note: including empty "validate" query parameter will cause the API to validate the payload and *not* make any changes in the system. The response to a "validate" request will either be HTTP 204 NO CONTENT indicating all the data is valid or HTTP 400 BAD REQUEST with a separate error for each invalid piece of data.

However, if the target group "A" has "closed" join policy, the group members should have "closed" join policies. If any of them have "open" join policy, the request to add members will be denied.         - membership type INTERNAL

      **OKTA**:
        - membership type INTERNAL
        - membership type EXTERNAL

        - unsupported target type

  5. The group must have no pending or in progress requests to ensure all changes are reflected in the target system.

post.description:
Join or request membership in existing groups by their ids.
The endpoint supports adding users other than the requestor to the groups.
If the user is not eligible to be a member, the request will be denied. If a group is open, the membership will be approved implicitly. If a group is closed, the membership will be requested on behalf of the user. If the requestor is the owner of a group in the list, the user will be added with implicit approval.
Optionally, provide a justification for adding a user as a member in the meta section of the request body.
Note: including empty "validate" query parameter will cause the API to validate the payload and *not* make any changes in the system. The response to a "validate" request will either be HTTP 204 NO CONTENT indicating all the data is valid or HTTP 400 BAD REQUEST with a separate error for each invalid piece of data.
